source.text: Οἱ δὲ κρατήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήγαγον πρὸς Καϊάφαν τὸν ἀρχιερέα, ὅπου οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι συνήχθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: Those and having seized the Jesus led away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered.

en.L: And those who had seized Jesus led [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders were gathered.
en.B: The men who had arrested Jesus took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to Caiaphas the high priest. The scribes and the elders had gathered there.
en.R: The men who arrested Jesus took {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the house of Caiaphas, the high priest. The teachers of the law and the older leaders were meeting there.

decisions.choice: where the scribes and the elders were gathered: the council met at night in the high priest's house
decisions.reason: The same place as in 26:3. A further meeting at dawn followed (27:1).

decisions.choice: the house of
decisions.reason: Readable says where they took him, as 26:58 shows.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἕως τῆς αὐλῆς τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, καὶ εἰσελθὼν ἔσω ἐκάθητο μετὰ τῶν ὑπηρετῶν ἰδεῖν τὸ τέλος.

records.literal_gloss: The and Peter was following him from afar up to the courtyard of the high priest, and having entered inside he was sitting with the attendants to see the end.

en.L: And Peter was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from a distance, as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and going inside, he sat with the guards to see the outcome.
en.B: Peter kept {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in sight from far behind and came as far as the high priest's courtyard. He went inside and took a seat among the guards, waiting to see what the end would be.
en.R: Peter followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, staying far behind. He came to the courtyard of the high priest's house. He went in and sat with the guards. He wanted to see what would happen to Jesus.

decisions.choice: guards: attendants, the temple police and servants of the high priest
decisions.reason: The word is used of officers who serve a court or an official.

decisions.choice: the outcome: how the matter would end
decisions.reason: Peter wants to know what will be done to Jesus.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ τὸ συνέδριον ὅλον ἐζήτουν ψευδομαρτυρίαν κατὰ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ὅπως αὐτὸν θανατώσωσιν, καὶ οὐχ εὗρον πολλῶν προσελθόντων ψευδομαρτύρων.

records.literal_gloss: The and chief priests and the council whole were seeking false testimony against the Jesus so that him they might put to death, \v 60 and not they found, many having come forward false witnesses.

en.L: Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking false testimony against Jesus so that they might put {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to death, \v 60 and they did not find [any], though many false witnesses came forward.
en.B: Meanwhile the chief priests and the whole council were trying to find false charges against Jesus that would get {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} executed. \v 60 Many false witnesses came forward, yet they found none.
en.R: The leading priests and the whole council wanted to kill Jesus. So they tried to find people who would tell lies about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 60 Many people came and told lies, but the council could not find anything to use against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: the council: the Sanhedrin, the highest Jewish court in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: It had about seventy members, chief priests, elders and scribes, with the high priest presiding.

decisions.choice: they did not find any: no testimony that would hold
alternatives: no one was willing to testify
decisions.reason: The law required two or three witnesses who agreed (Deuteronomy 19:15). Mark 14:56 says their testimony did not agree.

decisions.choice: anything to use against him
decisions.reason: Readable says what they failed to find.

source.text: ὕστερον δὲ προσελθόντες δύο εἶπαν· Οὗτος ἔφη· Δύναμαι καταλῦσαι τὸν ναὸν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ διὰ τριῶν ἡμερῶν οἰκοδομῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: Later and having come two \v 61 said, This one said, I am able to destroy the temple of the God and through three days to build.

en.L: But later two came forward \v 61 [and] said, "This [man] said, 'I am able to destroy the temple of God and to build [it] in three days.'"
en.B: At last two of them stepped up \v 61 and stated, "This man claimed, 'I am able to tear down the temple of God and build it again within three days.'"
en.R: At last two men came forward. \v 61 They said, "This man said, 'I can destroy God's temple and build it again in three days.'"

decisions.choice: two: the number of witnesses the law required
decisions.reason: Two agreeing witnesses were needed to convict (Deuteronomy 19:15).

decisions.choice: destroy the temple and build it in three days: a twisted form of Jesus's words
decisions.reason: Matthew records no such saying, though Jesus foretold the temple's destruction (24:2) and his rising on the third day. John 2:19 has Jesus say, "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up."

decisions.choice: temple: the sanctuary itself
decisions.reason: The word means the holy house of God, not the courts around it.

source.text: καὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Οὐδὲν ἀποκρίνῃ;

records.literal_gloss: And having stood up the high priest said to him, Nothing you answer?

en.L: And the high priest stood up and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} answer nothing?
en.B: Then the high priest stood up and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} no answer?
en.R: Then the high priest stood up and said to Jesus, "Do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} have nothing to say?

decisions.choice: two questions: "Do you answer nothing? What is it these testify?"
alternatives: one question: Do you answer nothing to what these testify against you?
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads two questions. The meaning is nearly the same either way.

source.text: τί οὗτοί σου καταμαρτυροῦσιν;

records.literal_gloss: What these you testify against?

en.L: What is it that these testify against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.B: What about the evidence these men are bringing against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.R: What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} say about these things they are saying against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"

decisions.choice: What about the evidence (B); What do you say about (R)
alternatives: What is it that these testify
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear that the high priest is pressing Jesus to reply.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐσιώπα.

records.literal_gloss: The and Jesus was silent.

en.L: But Jesus kept silent.
en.B: Jesus, however, said nothing.
en.R: But Jesus did not say anything.

decisions.choice: kept silent: like the servant of Isaiah 53:7
decisions.reason: The servant "did not open his mouth" before those who afflicted him. Matthew does not cite the verse here.

source.text: καὶ ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἐξορκίζω σε κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος ἵνα ἡμῖν εἴπῃς εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And the high priest said to him, I adjure you by the God the living that to us you say if you are the Christ the Son of the God.

en.L: And the high priest said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "I put {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} under oath by the living God that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} tell us whether {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of God."
en.B: Then the high priest said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "In the name of the living God I place {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} under oath. Tell us: are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of God?"
en.R: The high priest said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Swear by the living God and tell us: Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the Son of God?"

decisions.choice: I put you under oath: a formal demand that he answer before God
decisions.reason: Someone put under oath was bound to speak (Leviticus 5:1). Jesus, who had kept silent, now answers.

decisions.choice: the Christ, the Son of God: the Messiah, God's chosen king
decisions.reason: God called Israel's king his son (Psalm 2:7; 2 Samuel 7:14). The high priest uses the words of the confession Peter made (16:16).

decisions.choice: Swear by the living God and tell us
alternatives: I put you under oath by the living God
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what being put under oath means.

source.text: λέγει αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Σὺ εἶπας· πλὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἀπ’ ἄρτι ὄψεσθε τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καθήμενον ἐκ δεξιῶν τῆς δυνάμεως καὶ ἐρχόμενον ἐπὶ τῶν νεφελῶν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Says to him the Jesus, You said; yet I say to you, from now you will see the Son of the Man sitting at right of the Power and coming on the clouds of the heaven.

en.L: Jesus says to him, "You have said [so]. But I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at [the] right hand of the Power and coming on the clouds of heaven."
en.B: Jesus answered him, "You have said it yourself. Yet this I tell you all: from this time on, you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power, and coming on the clouds of heaven."
en.R: Jesus said to him, "You have said it yourself. But I tell all of you: After this you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right side of God, the Power. And you will see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} coming on the clouds of heaven."

decisions.choice: you have said so: yes, but in your words
decisions.reason: As in 26:25. Jesus accepts the title but goes on to say in his own words who he is.

decisions.choice: seated at the right hand, coming on the clouds: Psalm 110:1 and Daniel 7:13
decisions.reason: In Psalm 110:1 the Lord tells David's lord to sit at his right hand. In Daniel 7:13 one like a son of man comes with the clouds of heaven to receive a kingdom. Jesus joins the two (compare 22:44 and 24:30).

decisions.choice: the Power: a reverent way of saying God
decisions.reason: Jews often avoided saying God's name and spoke of him by titles such as this.

decisions.choice: from now on: from this point his exaltation begins
alternatives: only at the end of the age
decisions.reason: The "you" is plural. His judges will see him exalted, beginning with his death and resurrection and completed when he comes.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

decisions.choice: God, the Power
decisions.reason: Readable says who "the Power" is.

source.text: τότε ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς διέρρηξεν τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ἐβλασφήμησεν· τί ἔτι χρείαν ἔχομεν μαρτύρων;

records.literal_gloss: Then the high priest tore the garments of him saying, He blasphemed; why still need have we of witnesses?

en.L: Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, "He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses?
en.B: The high priest then ripped his robes and cried, "This is blasphemy! What use do we have for more witnesses?
en.R: Then the high priest tore his clothes to show how upset he was. He said, "He has insulted God! We do not need any more witnesses!

decisions.choice: tore his garments: a sign of grief and horror
decisions.reason: People tore their clothes on hearing words against God (2 Kings 18:37-19:1).

decisions.choice: blasphemed: insulted God by claiming what belongs to God
decisions.reason: As in 9:3. To claim a seat at God's right hand was, to the high priest, a claim to share God's honor (Leviticus 24:16).

decisions.choice: to show how upset he was
decisions.reason: Readable explains the gesture.

source.text: ἴδε νῦν ἠκούσατε τὴν βλασφημίαν·

records.literal_gloss: Behold now you heard the blasphemy.

en.L: Look, now you have heard the blasphemy.
en.B: You have now heard the blasphemy yourselves.
en.R: You all just heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} insult God.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.

decisions.choice: heard him insult God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word, as in 26:65.

source.text: τί ὑμῖν δοκεῖ;

records.literal_gloss: What to you seems?

en.L: What do you think?"
en.B: What is your verdict?"
en.R: What do you decide?"

decisions.choice: what do you think: a call for a verdict
decisions.reason: The high priest asks the council to decide (compare Mark 14:64).

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἀποκριθέντες εἶπαν· Ἔνοχος θανάτου ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: They and answering said, Liable of death he is.

en.L: And they answered and said, "He is deserving of death."
en.B: They answered, "He deserves to die."
en.R: They answered, "He should be put to death!"

decisions.choice: deserving of death: guilty of a crime that carries the death penalty
decisions.reason: The law punished blasphemy with death (Leviticus 24:16). Under Roman rule the council could not carry out a death sentence itself, so they hand Jesus to Pilate (27:1-2; John 18:31).

source.text: τότε ἐνέπτυσαν εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐκολάφισαν αὐτόν, οἱ δὲ ἐράπισαν λέγοντες· Προφήτευσον ἡμῖν, χριστέ, τίς ἐστιν ὁ παίσας σε;

records.literal_gloss: Then they spat into the face of him and struck him, others and slapped \v 68 saying, Prophesy to us, Christ, who is the one having struck you?

en.L: Then they spat in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face and struck {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and others slapped [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], \v 68 saying, "Prophesy to us, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}! Who is it that struck {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.B: Next they spat in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face and pounded {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with their fists, while others struck {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with open hands \v 68 and jeered, "Prophesy for us, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}! Which one of us hit {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}?"
en.R: Then some of them spat in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} face and hit {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with their fists. Others slapped {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 68 They said, "Show us {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are a prophet, {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}! Tell us who hit {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}!"

decisions.choice: they: members of the council, and perhaps the guards with them
decisions.reason: Matthew does not say who; Mark 14:65 adds the guards.

decisions.choice: prophesy, who struck you: a mocking test of a prophet
decisions.reason: Mark 14:65 and Luke 22:64 say they covered his face. Matthew does not mention it, but the taunt assumes he could not see who hit him.

decisions.choice: spitting and striking: Isaiah 50:6
decisions.reason: The servant says, "I did not hide my face from shame and spitting." Jesus had foretold this mocking (20:19).

decisions.choice: Show us you are a prophet
decisions.reason: Readable says what the taunt demands.

source.text: Ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐκάθητο ἔξω ἐν τῇ αὐλῇ· καὶ προσῆλθεν αὐτῷ μία παιδίσκη λέγουσα· Καὶ σὺ ἦσθα μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Γαλιλαίου·

records.literal_gloss: The and Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard; and came to him one servant girl saying, Also you were with Jesus the Galilean.

en.L: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came to him, saying, "You too were with Jesus the Galilean."
en.B: Meanwhile Peter was sitting out in the courtyard. A servant girl came up to him and said, "You were with Jesus the Galilean too."
en.R: Peter was still sitting outside in the courtyard. A young woman who worked there came to him. She said, "You were with Jesus, the man from Galilee!"

decisions.choice: servant girl: a young female slave or servant of the household
decisions.reason: She belonged to the high priest's household.

decisions.choice: outside: in the open courtyard, outside the room where Jesus was being tried
decisions.reason: Peter had come inside the gate (26:58); the trial went on in the house.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἠρνήσατο ἔμπροσθεν πάντων λέγων· Οὐκ οἶδα τί λέγεις.

records.literal_gloss: He and denied before all saying, Not I know what you say.

en.L: But he denied [it] before them all, saying, "I do not know what you are saying."
en.B: But Peter denied it with everyone listening. "I have no idea what you mean," he said.
en.R: But Peter said in front of everyone, "I do not know what you are talking about!"

decisions.choice: I do not know what you are saying: a way of brushing off the charge
decisions.reason: Peter pretends not to understand rather than answer.

decisions.choice: before them all: a public denial
decisions.reason: Compare 10:33: whoever denies Jesus before people.

source.text: ἐξελθόντα δὲ εἰς τὸν πυλῶνα εἶδεν αὐτὸν ἄλλη καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἐκεῖ· Οὗτος ἦν μετὰ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου·

records.literal_gloss: Having gone out and to the gateway saw him another and says to those there, This one was with Jesus the Nazarene.

en.L: And when he had gone out to the gateway, another [servant girl] saw him and says to those there, "This [man] was with Jesus the Nazarene."
en.B: He went out toward the gateway, where another servant girl saw him and told the people there, "This man was with Jesus of Nazareth."
en.R: Then Peter went out to the gate. Another servant girl saw him there. She said to the people standing there, "This man was with Jesus from Nazareth."

decisions.choice: the Nazarene: the man from Nazareth
decisions.reason: Jesus grew up in Nazareth (2:23).

decisions.choice: the gateway: the entrance passage from the street into the courtyard
decisions.reason: Peter moves away from the fire toward the way out.

decisions.choice: present tense of narration (L); past (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek present tense of narration.

source.text: καὶ πάλιν ἠρνήσατο μετὰ ὅρκου ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

records.literal_gloss: And again he denied with an oath, Not I know the man.

en.L: And again he denied [it] with an oath, "I do not know the man."
en.B: Again he denied it, this time with an oath: "I do not know the man!"
en.R: Again Peter said it was not true. He made a promise before God and said, "I do not know that man!"

decisions.choice: with an oath: calling on God as witness
decisions.reason: An oath called on God to confirm one's words. Jesus had taught his disciples not to swear at all (5:34-37).

decisions.choice: the man: Peter will not even say Jesus's name
decisions.reason: He speaks of Jesus as a stranger.

decisions.choice: made a promise before God
decisions.reason: Readable explains what an oath is.

source.text: μετὰ μικρὸν δὲ προσελθόντες οἱ ἑστῶτες εἶπον τῷ Πέτρῳ· Ἀληθῶς καὶ σὺ ἐξ αὐτῶν εἶ, καὶ γὰρ ἡ λαλιά σου δῆλόν σε ποιεῖ·

records.literal_gloss: After a little and having come those standing said to the Peter, Truly also you of them are, also for the speech of you evident you makes.

en.L: And after a little [while], those standing [there] came and said to Peter, "Truly you too are [one] of them, for even your speech makes you evident."
en.B: Before long the people standing nearby came up to Peter. "You are certainly one of them," they said. "The way you talk betrays you."
en.R: A little later, the people standing there came to Peter. They said, "We are sure you are one of Jesus's followers. We can tell from the way you talk that you are from Galilee."

decisions.choice: your speech: Peter's Galilean way of speaking
decisions.reason: Galileans spoke with an accent that people in Jerusalem could recognize. Jesus and his disciples were known to come from Galilee (26:69).

decisions.choice: one of Jesus's followers; that you are from Galilee
alternatives: one of them; your speech makes you evident
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" are and what his speech showed.

source.text: τότε ἤρξατο καταθεματίζειν καὶ ὀμνύειν ὅτι Οὐκ οἶδα τὸν ἄνθρωπον.

records.literal_gloss: Then he began to curse and to swear, Not I know the man.

en.L: Then he began to call down curses and to swear, "I do not know the man!"
en.B: Then he began cursing and swearing, "I do not know the man!"
en.R: Then Peter began to curse. He swore an oath and said, "I do not know the man!"

decisions.choice: to call down curses: probably on himself if he was lying
decisions.reason: The verb means to invoke a curse, but Matthew does not say on whom. It may be on himself, as an oath of denial, or on Jesus.

decisions.choice: the third denial is the strongest
alternatives: the same as the first two
decisions.reason: A plain denial (26:70), then an oath (26:72), now curses and an oath.

source.text: καὶ εὐθέως ἀλέκτωρ ἐφώνησεν·

records.literal_gloss: And immediately a rooster crowed.

en.L: And immediately a rooster crowed.
en.B: At that very moment a rooster crowed.
en.R: Right then a rooster crowed.

decisions.choice: immediately: the sign Jesus foretold comes at once
decisions.reason: The crowing comes just as Peter finishes his third denial (26:34).

source.text: καὶ ἐμνήσθη ὁ Πέτρος τοῦ ῥήματος Ἰησοῦ εἰρηκότος ὅτι Πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι τρὶς ἀπαρνήσῃ με, καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἔξω ἔκλαυσεν πικρῶς.

records.literal_gloss: And remembered the Peter the word of Jesus having said, Before rooster to crow three times you will deny me; and having gone outside he wept bitterly.

en.L: And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, who had said, "Before a rooster crows, you will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times." And he went outside and wept bitterly.
en.B: Then Peter remembered what Jesus had told him: "Before a rooster crows, you will deny {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} three times." And he went outside and broke down in bitter tears.
en.R: Peter remembered what Jesus had said: "Before the rooster crows, you will say three times that you do not know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}." Peter went outside and cried very hard.

decisions.choice: the word of Jesus: his warning in 26:34, now fulfilled
decisions.reason: Matthew repeats the words of 26:34 so the reader sees them come true.

decisions.choice: wept bitterly: deep grief over what he had done
decisions.reason: Peter's sorrow stands in contrast with Judas's end (27:3-5).

decisions.choice: broke down in bitter tears
decisions.reason: Balanced uses current English with the same force.
